offer.scope: staging/test authority mapping, up to 3 integrations, 10-20 scenarios, evidence pack and retest

research_limitations.basis: current connected Gmail evidence plus existing Control Center commercial truth
research_limitations.rule: Do not infer unverified current product/security claims beyond the cited mailbox evidence; refresh public web before SEND.

evidence: 2026-08-05 mailbox evidence: VentureVerse reports 25+ live AI apps for operators and a product aimed at doing operator work.
Earlier mailbox evidence identifies named VentureVerse/OG Club community leadership and Brinc acquisition/transition context.
Publication email explicitly invites replies about what the reader is building.
targets.pain_hypothesis: A multi-app operator stack creates permission, tool-action, evidence, failure-boundary and human-gate sprawl across many AI surfaces.
targets.contact_path: Reply to The Operator Stack / VentureVerse publication; route to product/operator leadership. No personal email address stored in this queue.
targets.hook: You are selling a stack of AI apps to operators; we can map what each app/agent is actually allowed to do, where human gates exist, and what evidence proves safe execution before those workflows scale.
targets.next: Refresh public product/security surface, then prepare one concise founder/product-team outreach draft.

evidence: Mailbox history shows repeated GYG Agency AI/Web3 events including The 90-Day AI Playbook.
GYG promoted OneAgent Night Bangkok with live AI trading and participant community access.
Organizer messages explicitly permit reply-to-organizer contact; an official Telegram participant/community path exists.
targets.pain_hypothesis: Client-facing AI/Web3 delivery plus live-agent/financial-adjacent demonstrations create a strong need to separate marketing claims from verified agent permissions, approvals, logs and effect boundaries.
targets.contact_path: Reply to GYG organizer event email or use the existing official GYG Telegram community path; exact destination must be re-read before SEND.
targets.hook: You already teach and showcase AI implementation. The audit gives you a concrete trust artifact: what an agent can do, which actions require approval, what was actually logged, and where claims outrun evidence.
targets.next: Select one current GYG/OneAgent workflow or client-facing automation as the audit wedge; draft message only after public refresh.

evidence: 2026-07 mailbox evidence shows cyber•Fund running the recurring Building AI-Native Startups series with named founders/builders.
Event email explicitly permits replying to the organizer.
targets.pain_hypothesis: An AI-native startup portfolio needs a repeatable diligence layer for agent authority, tool access, approval gates and evidence quality before portfolio companies move from demo to pilot/production.
targets.contact_path: Reply to the cyber•Fund event organizer and position the audit as a one-company portfolio pilot, not a broad consulting retainer.
targets.hook: For AI-native startups, the hidden diligence gap is not model quality but effect authority: what the agent can touch, what requires a human, and whether the logs actually prove the claimed controls.
targets.next: Refresh current portfolio/program context; pick one portfolio-company pilot framing and prepare a short partner-facing draft.

The same email describes AI expense review with issue flagging and approval routing.
targets.pain_hypothesis: Orchestrator/sub-agent delegation and approval-routing are exact authority-boundary surfaces: delegation scope, tool permissions, approval bypass, evidence completeness and replayability.
targets.contact_path: Current mailbox path is marketing/event/Care, not a qualified buyer contact. Proper product/security/partnership contact must be found before SEND.
targets.hook: Your own Sub-Agent framing already centers trust and debugging. We would test the next layer: whether delegated actions, approval requirements and evidence are actually enforceable and reconstructable across integrations.
targets.next: Find a legitimate product/security/partnership contact; do not pitch through Care/support.

reserves.evidence: Prior first-party mailbox incident documents a Manus task malfunction while interacting with Google Drive, deleted/moved a working folder, broke the workflow, and left the user asking for an action log/explanation.
reserves.rule: Do not repurpose the old support thread or support staff as a sales channel. Only use a proper current product/security/partnership contact if independently found.

reserves.evidence: 2026-08 mailbox evidence says Zapier is positioning itself as an AI orchestration platform and exposes Zapier MCP to an ecosystem of 9,000+ integrations; a demo-team path exists.
reserves.rule: Do not misuse an inbound demo booking flow as a sales pitch. Find the correct product/security/partnership route first.

selection_rule: Prioritize evidence-backed fit plus a legitimate reply/organizer path. Do not send to support, no-reply, or unrelated demo funnels. Refresh public current facts before any outreach.
